- **P7 (confirmatory test of the exploratory S_adj; rule fixed here before it is run).** S_adj is an exploratory post-hoc variant (S² minus the expected noise part, from the null simulation), chosen after seeing the partial results, and may not be a finding without a test on data not used to choose it. **Definition frozen now**: S_adj as implemented in `analysis/make_diag.py` (`Sadj_h1`), **with the noise part taken from a parametric-bootstrap null on the reporting fit** (outcomes redrawn from the fitted reporting specification with residual variance σ̂², so that S_adj is computable from one experiment; the current version uses the null column of the same run with the true noise ratio). Its coefficients (the fitted combination with the corner term) are **frozen from the original cells and applied without refitting**. **Confirmatory set** (never used to choose S_adj): new seeds and new graph draws for mechanisms (a)–(f); mechanism (g) (convex mirror) with the full p grid; and two graph families not in the current list: a clustered scale-free graph (Holme–Kim / power-law cluster) and a configuration-model graph with log-normal degrees (the analysis may substitute a comparable pair and says so); core d ∈ {5, 20, 80}, p ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}, Tier G only. **Pass rule:** supported if, on the confirmatory set, (1) the absolute held-out R² of log|bias| from the frozen S_adj-based score is > 0 (it must beat the constant, not only a benchmark), (2) its gain over the best benchmark is ≥ 0.05 with the group-level bootstrap CI excluding 0, and (3) the gain is positive in at least two thirds of the held-out groups (mechanisms (a)–(g) and the two new families). Inconclusive if (1) holds but the CI includes 0; otherwise not supported. The result is reported next to the 

## Contribution over prior work
Chin 2019 and Han–Ugander 2023 propose the estimators, show they can work, and (Chin) point out the feature-distribution mismatch qualitatively; Gao–Ding 2023 study regression estimators of exposure-mapping estimands under overlap; the design-based literature (Aronow–Samii, Ugander et al., Eckles et al., Leung, Li–Wager) analyses HT/Hájek with specified exposures. What is open, and what this study provides: a quantified decomposition of regression-GATE error into leverage variance and extrapolation bias with different, separately tested scalings in n, d, p, design; the interaction with cluster randomization; fair tiered comparisons with the exposure-mapping family; a data-computable two-part diagnostic with a pre-registered acceptance rule against trivial predictors; the regimes where DM beats regression; and whether flexible/graph learners help. Claimed "to our knowledge within the literature checked". Not a new estimator; a verified, predictive account of when to trust an existing one. Headline emphasis (after review): the design × estimator × regime map and the regimes where regression loses, with the diagnostic as a pre-registered test — not P1, which is a textbook identity used as the reference.

## Study design (what the idea asks of the analysis)
- **Estimand**: GATE τ = mean_i[Y_i(1)] − mean_i[Y_i(0)], exact in simulation (noise-free outcome function at the corners).
- **Calibration**: every mechanism is calibrated to a common τ (=1, outcome SD of the noise-free part scaled accordingly) and a common spillover share s = (τ − τ_direct)/τ ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75} (mechanism-independent definition of interference strength). Errors are normalised by this fixed τ (no division by a near-zero effect); sign-error rate retained; the DM bias per cell is reported so the calibration is checkable. σ is a multiple of the SD of the noise-free outcome, which under calibration to τ=1 depends on mechanism and s: the resulting signal-to-noise (τ/σ and the variance share of the noise) is tabulated per mechanism × s, so noise levels are comparable across mechanisms.
- **Networks**: synthetic ER/SBM/BA/Watts–Strogatz, n ∈ 10^3–10^4, mean degree ~5–100

shown.message:
Outline rev 9 is pushed. It applies Brief rev. 8 (P5 verdict wording, P7, exact formula vs expansion).

- **P5 wording:** part (i) is supported on the discriminating cells. Part (ii) is refuted only for the bias scores we tried. The diagnostic reduces to a variance diagnostic plus the assumption-indexed interval (C9). The text leads with the absolute held-out R² result (every data-computable predictor below a constant) and says what the interval does and does not exclude.
- **New C6b (P7):** a confirmatory test of the exploratory S_adj, with the pass rule fixed before running. It needs new runs. If `analysis` doesn't run it, the paper says S_adj was exploratory and untested.
- **C2:** the bias predictor in the tests is the exact population-OLS limit, not the second-order expansion.

I also checked the paper draft's abstract, results §3.4 and discussion against the outline. The results text already matches the outline: it has the "no evidence" wording, absolute R², the (e) 58% and the 0.55 exponent. Three wordings go beyond the evidence, so I opened `paper-repo`#5. They are:
- "No score computed from the data predicts the bias" should say "none of the scores we tried".
- The flexible-learners claim needs its scope: 12–14 cells per mechanism, fixed tunings, and (d) as an exception.
- The abstract should say the data do not identify the bias, as an interpretation.

`report` decides the text. I also updated `story-repo`#2.

Still waiting on `analysis` (`experiment-repo`#6/#7) and `presentation` (`figtab-repo`#3). `story-repo`#2 stays open.
